neighbours.label: being fussy or overly particular about small details (quibble, pedantic, nitpick, insist on)
fire: Sorry to be pedantic, but the meeting is on Tuesday, not Monday.
We spent an hour quibbling about the colour of the new logo.
My editor loves to nitpick every comma in my articles.
He was fussy about the exact temperature of his morning tea.
The judge was scrupulous about following each rule to the letter.
She kept insisting on the precise wording of the contract.
I hate to split hairs, but that figure is off by two percent.
Our coach was a stickler for perfectly straight lines at practice.
quiet: Sorry to interrupt, but the meeting is on Tuesday, not Monday.
We spent an hour talking about the colour of the new logo.
My editor loves to read every chapter of my articles.
He was happy with the warm temperature of his morning tea.
The judge was tired after following the long trial all day.
She kept reading the final wording of the contract.
I hate to say it, but that figure is up by two percent.
Our coach was a fan of long runs at practice.

notes: Top examples: 'bothers me', 'quibble over', 'scrupulously accurate', 'insisting on', 'beat yourself up', 'pedantic'. Logit effect of the + direction suppresses precise/insisting/stubborn/strict, so the - pole promotes them. Probe: pedantic 0.67, quibble 1.06, the plain sentence 0.0.
